\newcommand{\ResultsAbstract}{A solver reads \EoneInD\% to \EoneInA\% of its own hardening level but at most \EoneGoneMax\% of another generator, and 100 labels of the new scheme give \EtwoGtwoGoneFtHundred\% in one direction and \EtwoGoneGtwoFtHundred\% in the other. Adversarial perturbation at $\epsilon=16/255$ leaves an independent solver at \EthreeTrSixteen\%, and fine-tuning restores \EthreeFtSixteen\%. Zero-shot local VLMs read \VlmAccQwenC\% (Qwen3.5) and \VlmAccGemmaC\% (Gemma~3) of CAPTCHAs at hardening level L2. In simulated per-key streams of held-out participants, the monitor flags every direct solver at an estimated false-positive rate of \EfiveHumNoSixFifty\% without its dispersion property, and at \EfiveHumFifty\% with it (\EfiveHumRangeFifty\% across splits), which also flags \EfivePoolFullFifty\% of bots that replay pooled human latencies. These are model-based estimates, not measurements of observed long sessions. A bot that samples a per-person latency model is limited only by the rate bound, \TputBound{} solves per key and hour at one challenge per five minutes.}
\newcommand{\DiscussionSolverSentence}{A solver that fails on a new scheme reaches \EtwoGtwoGoneFtHundred\% (G2 to G1) or \EtwoGoneGtwoFtHundred\% (G1 to G2) after fine-tuning on 100 labels. A zero-shot local VLM reads \VlmAccQwenC\% (Qwen3.5) or \VlmAccGemmaC\% (Gemma~3) of L2 CAPTCHAs without any training.}
\newcommand{\ConclusionRQThree}{Hardening protects only against solvers trained on another level or scheme. A solver trained on the deployed level reads \EoneInD\% to \EoneInA\% of it, 100 labels of a new scheme lift transfer to \EtwoGtwoGoneFtHundred\% (G2 to G1) or \EtwoGoneGtwoFtHundred\% (G1 to G2), and adversarial perturbation that removes the defender's own solver leaves an independent one at \EthreeTrSixteen\% at $\epsilon=16/255$, which fine-tuning raises to \EthreeFtSixteen\%. Zero-shot local VLMs read \VlmAccQwenC\% and \VlmAccGemmaC\% of L2 CAPTCHAs. These are solver-resistance results, since human solving of G2 was not measured.}
